_meta.purpose: Immutable, append-only ledger of pre-committed OPERATIONAL-CAPACITY and ASCERTAINMENT forecasts for the BDBV 2026 outbreak. Sibling to data/calibration-ledger.json, which holds corridor pins. Separate because the corridor ledger's point identity is derived from (source, target) and an operational pin has neither; forcing one into that schema would break refresh_pipeline._calibration_point_id verification.
doctrine: Pin once. A block's pins, probabilities, pin date and resolution date are never edited after commit.

Generated, never authored. Every probability is produced by lovs/forecast/pins.build_pins() from the frozen operational series. tests/test_operational_ledger.py re-runs the generator and asserts the committed values match, so a hand-edited probability fails the suite.
Append only. New pins are a NEW block at an explicit pin moment, never a mutation of an existing one.
Resolve by appending. On the resolution date, score each pin against the refreshed series and append the outcome; the pinned probability is never altered.

One observable per pin. Pins sharing a metric sit at different thresholds or shapes, so no two resolve from the same boolean. This is the defect that made the first draft of corridor Block 5 unscoreable.
A NO requires coverage. A pin resolves NO only when the series reaches its resolution date; a series that stops short returns unscoreable_stale_series.

errata.correction: The block rationale states that isolation occupancy 'has risen monotonically to 896'. That is FALSE. Over 80 observations the series moves up 51 times, down 24 and flat 4, with a single-day fall of -146 on 2026-08-11. The pinned probability is UNAFFECTED: the bootstrap resamples the observed day-over-day changes, so it read the falls even though the prose did not. Independently re-priced from the committed ledger fields at a different seed, iso-below-850 and iso-above-1000 reproduce to 0.1285 and 0.5895, and both residuals sit inside two combined Monte Carlo standard errors, so the pins are properties of the series rather than of seed 6001. The original rationale is left as written because a pinned block is immutable; this erratum is the correction of record, and a scorer should read it alongside.

LIMITATION FOUND AFTER PINNING, recorded rather than repaired, because repairing it would mean re-pinning. The national isolation series is a sum over a province panel whose membership changes between SitReps. Holding the panel constant across each day-pair cuts day-over-day standard deviation from 62.7 to 35.7 while the drift survives (+8.7 to +8.5), so on that decomposition roughly two thirds of the variance is province reporting churn rather than clinical movement; a cruder whole-series decomposition puts it higher still. The worst single artifact is 2026-08-12, raw +312 against a constant-panel +63. The consequence for these two pins is directional and known: the bootstrap resamples that churn as if it were ward movement, so the simulated spread is WIDER than the underlying process warrants, which pushes both probabilities toward 0.5. The fix is a panel-stable series in the extract, and it belongs to a future block, not this one.

The registration note cites walk-forward skill of +0.198 (Brier 0.1996 against a base-rate 0.2489 over 450 forecasts). That backtest truncated history on DATA day, not PUBLICATION day. A packet describing data day D is published on D+1, so truncating on the data day hands the backtest one publication lag of information it would not have had: a genuine one-lag look-ahead. Re-run with publication-day truncation over the same 450 forecasts, Brier is 0.1870 and skill is +0.2486. The bias therefore ran in the CONSERVATIVE direction -- the cited figure understated the forecaster rather than overstating it, most likely because anchoring the bootstrap on a one-day-older level is less sensitive to the latest noisy observation. No pinned probability is affected: the pins are generated from the full series as of 2026-09-01 and involve no backtest. The registration note is left as written because a pinned block is immutable; +0.2486 is the corrected figure of record.
errata.found_by: lovs/forecast/cadenceintegrity.py, which found the same class of bug in its own build

blocks.rationale:
Block 6, and the first operational block. Registered the same day corridor Block 5 was pinned rather than a month later, because pre-registration cannot be backfilled and a month of waiting is a month that can never be scored.

WHY OPERATIONAL RATHER THAN SPATIAL. The corridor model has saturated: its target-level union hazard is 1.000000 for every eligible target, so it cannot produce a discriminating spatial forecast at the current burden. Corridor Block 5 pins that saturation as a falsification test. This block goes where discrimination still exists. Contact follow-up carries 81 observations and moved 7 to 87 percent; lab positivity carries 66 and fell 46 to 14 percent while confirmed cases grew sixtyfold. These are real series with real uncertainty, and nobody forecasts them.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FORECASTING AT ALL. Everyone forecasts the virus. The response system's own degradation is slower-moving and therefore more forecastable, it is actionable in a way transmission is not, and it decides whether anyone's case numbers mean anything. It is also the empirical core of the ascertainment and blind-spot work.

SPREAD. 12 pins across 6 metrics spanning predicted 0.129 to 0.744, in six bands. The corridor ledger's 19 resolved pins span 0.230 to 0.459 across 12 distinct events and the resolver reports them as effectively a single bin. This block is the first that can produce a reliability curve.

TWO DELIBERATE BIAS TESTS. The walk-forward backtest measured the forecaster overconfident at the low end: forecasts priced 0.05 occurred 23 percent of the time and forecasts priced 0.15 occurred 42 percent. Rather than silently correcting the model output, two pins (iso-below-850 at 0.129 and cft-below-70 at 0.180) commit the model's own low numbers so the resolution measures whether that bias is real and persistent.
blocks.registration_note:
Pinned 2026-09-01 on founder go-signal, NOT backdated. Every probability is generated by lovs/forecast/pins.build_pins() from data/operational-series-2026-09-01.json, a frozen extract of 101 INSP/INRB SitRep packets covering 2026-05-14 to 2026-08-28. No probability is authored, and a test re-runs the generator to prove it.

METHOD. Stationary block bootstrap over day-over-day changes, 5-day blocks, 20000 paths, seeded per pin. Blocks rather than single days because these series are autocorrelated. Validated by walk-forward backtest: 450 forecasts, Brier 0.1996 against a base-rate Brier of 0.2489, skill +0.198; within the 0.15-0.85 band, skill +0.119 over 282 forecasts.

WHAT THE METHOD CANNOT SUPPORT, stated rather than hidden. The bootstrap encodes only how these series have moved. A structural break -- a funding cliff, a security incident closing a province, a change in reporting definition -- is outside it. Two metrics were considered and REJECTED for this block because the bootstrap prices them by extrapolating drift: confirmed_cfr_percent (which returned 1.000 for 'ever exceeds 50 percent' purely from upward drift in a ratio whose denominator is growing) and any 'ever crosses' question on a noisy daily series, which is dominated by single-day noise rather than signal.

LOOK-AHEAD AUDIT. The series ends 2026-08-28 and the window opens 2026-09-01, so no pin can be pre-resolved by in-window data: none exists yet. The four-day gap between the last observation and the pin date is the residual risk, and it runs in the conservative direction -- the forecaster is working from slightly older information than reality.

RESOLUTION. Re-extract the operational series from the SitRep packets so it covers 2026-10-01, then run lovs/forecast/opsresolver.py --as-of 2026-10-01. A pin whose series stops short returns unscoreable_stale_series rather than a false NO.

blocks.label: Block 7
blocks.rationale:
Block 7, pinned the same day as Blocks 5 and 6. Three blocks now run on one window. That is deliberate: pre-registration cannot be backfilled, the five operational modules finished today, and holding their questions for a later block would spend a month of scoreable time to gain nothing.

LARGELY INDEPENDENT OF BLOCK 6, WITH ONE STATED EXCEPTION. Block 6 pins contact follow-up, lab positivity, national isolation occupancy, new confirmed, health zones and alerts. Block 7 pins publication lag, PER-PROVINCE isolation, lab throughput, cumulative recovered, confirmed deaths per day and SitRep arrivals. Every level-bootstrap pin here resolves from a series no Block 6 pin touches. THE EXCEPTION is first-zero-case-day, which reads new_confirmed_today, a series Block 6 pins twice. It is a distinct observable -- 'any day reports zero' against 'the final day is at or below 60' and 'at or above 100', different shapes and different thresholds, so no two of the three resolve from one boolean -- but the three are CORRELATED, and a scorer must not treat them as three independent tests of the method. That pin is kept rather than dropped because it is the only low-band bias test available from a third method, and naming the correlation is more useful than losing the cross-method comparison.

THREE METHODS SCORED AGAINST EACH OTHER ON ONE WINDOW. Ten pins come from the level bootstrap over day-over-day changes. Two come from a GAP bootstrap over SitRep inter-arrival intervals, which is a different quantity and a different resampling scheme. One comes from the termination bootstrap, which carries a reflecting boundary at zero. No single-method block can tell you which approach is better calibrated; this one can.

SPREAD 0.137 TO 0.879, wider than Block 6, and specifically it reaches ABOVE 0.744, which Block 6 could not. The forecaster's calibration above three quarters is currently unmeasured; recovered-above-1700 at 0.879 is the pin that measures it.

TWO MORE LOW-BAND BIAS TESTS, from a different series and a different method than Block 6's pair. Four low-band pins across two blocks is the smallest set that can begin to say whether the measured overconfidence below 0.15 is a property of the METHOD or of one series.

WHY THESE QUESTIONS. Each comes from something a module found today. Publication lag is drifting (1.120 to 1.540 days between the first and second fifty packets, permutation p = 0.0005) and is the only degradation signal visible while the feed still delivers everything. Nord-Kivu is the province the CFR instrument flags as most likely under-ascertaining and the isolation module ranks second on pressure. Lab throughput ramped in batches rather than smoothly. Per-province isolation is used instead of national because roughly two thirds of the national series' day-over-day variance is province panel churn.
blocks.registration_note:
Pinned 2026-09-01 on founder go-signal, NOT backdated. Every probability is generated by lovs/forecast/pins_block7.build_pins() from data/operational-series-2026-09-01.json and the committed modules; a test re-runs the generator and asserts the ledger matches.

SEPARATE GENERATOR FROM BLOCK 6 on purpose: a pinned block's probabilities must regenerate exactly, and sharing a generator would couple the two blocks' stability.

publication_lag and per-province isolation are DERIVED series, not columns in the extract. Their derivations live in pins_block7.py and are covered by tests, so a scorer can reconstruct them.

NOT PINNED, and why. Declaration of the outbreak being over inside this window is a STRUCTURAL zero, not a small probability: 43 consecutive case-free days do not fit in 30. Pinning a structural impossibility would score a certainty as though it were a forecast. Haut-Uele isolation was considered and dropped: 19 observations is too thin for this bootstrap.

LOOK-AHEAD AUDIT. The series ends 2026-08-28 and the window opens 2026-09-01, so no pin can be pre-resolved: no in-window observation exists. The four-day gap runs conservative.

KNOWN INHERITED LIMITATION. The level bootstrap's cited backtest skill was computed with data-day truncation, a one-lag look-ahead; corrected to publication-day truncation the figure is Brier 0.1870, skill +0.2486 over the same 450 forecasts. See errata.

points.public_question: Does any SitRep data day between 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01 report zero new confirmed cases?
points.rationale: LOW-BAND BIAS TEST from a third method. The outbreak runs at 82 confirmed cases a day and has never recorded a zero day, so this is genuinely unlikely rather than artificially low. Reported on the reflecting variant: a plain difference bootstrap bounces off zero, which is why the module brackets rather than gives one number. Declaration inside this window is a STRUCTURAL zero, not a small probability, since 43 case-free days do not fit in 30, and is therefore not pinned.

generator.method: termination bootstrap, reflecting boundary at zero

points.public_question: Do at least 29 SitReps arrive between 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01?
points.rationale: Delivery volume, benchmarked on the last 30 days rather than chosen. The gap bootstrap structurally cannot draw a silence longer than the 3 days it resamples, so it prices variation inside a regime that has never broken and cannot price the regime breaking. That is the exact failure that cost this programme 58 days, and it is why this pin is worth having.

generator.method: stationary block bootstrap over 56 inter-arrival gaps from the last 60 days; 20000 paths, 5-day blocks, seed 20260901. Sustains = at least 29 arrivals and no silence longer than 2d, both benchmarked on the last 30 days. Bootstrap cannot draw a silence longer than 3d, and the record's worst is 3d

points.public_question: On the last SitRep data day on or before 2026-10-01, were 700 or more samples analysed that day?
points.rationale: Lab capacity. Throughput stands at 569. The ramp library found this pillar grew in batches, not smoothly: mean step +5.74 per day but median -4.00, with 30 days up against 35 down.

generator.method: stationary block bootstrap over day-over-day changes

points.public_question: Between 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01, does the SitRep feed avoid any silence longer than two consecutive days?
points.rationale: Feed continuity. The last 30 days ran 29 arrivals with no gap over 2, which is the top of this feed's range with no headroom. Method is a gap bootstrap, not a level bootstrap, so this pin scores a different approach on the same window.
